_note: Fact-sheet news writer set (eval/news-writer-set.mjs). Each case is an Event (news/CONTRACT.md) on a real tracked entry (entry_key in web/data/v2/entries.json), with facts taken from that entry's record unless marked constructed. bad: synthetic cards the code checks must refuse (they are replayed with a second reader that wrongly says faithful, so only code stands between them and the page). recorded: the live writer and reader answers, recorded once (node eval/news-writer-set.mjs --record) and replayed offline; review: the human-style verdict on the recorded AI card (ok | bad), made by reading it against the fact sheet.

writer.headline: Executive Order 14409 directs agencies on cyber benchmarks for frontier models
writer.body: The President signed Executive Order 14409 on June 2, 2026. It directs Treasury, the Department of War/NSA, and DHS/CISA, after consulting the White House, Commerce/NIST and others, to develop a classified cyber-capability benchmark and threshold for covered frontier models. It also directs them to design a voluntary developer framework.

writer.headline: Executive Order 14409 Directs Agencies on Classified Cyber Benchmark and Threshold
writer.body: On June 2, 2026, the President signed Executive Order 14409. It directs Treasury, the Department of War/NSA, and DHS/CISA, consulting the White House, Commerce/NIST and others, to develop a classified cyber-capability benchmark and threshold for covered frontier models. It also directs them to design a voluntary developer framework permitting pre-release access.

added_or_overstated: The card says the order directs them to 'design a voluntary developer framework' while the fact sheet says the framework is one 'permitting' pre-release access; the card omits the stated purpose, so the framework's function is not conveyed as the fact sheet describes it.

The headline describes the order as directing agencies on 'cyber benchmarks for frontier models', which is a characterisation not stated in the fact sheet beyond the benchmark and threshold directive.

facts.title: AI chip licensing to China and Macau

bad.headline: Commerce Department issues final AI chip rule

writer.headline: Bureau of Industry and Security issues final rule on AI chip licensing to China and Macau
writer.body: The Bureau of Industry and Security issued a final rule on January 15, 2026, covering AI chip licensing to China and Macau. The rule provides case-by-case review for certain US exports of chips below specified performance and memory-bandwidth limits, including H200 and MI325X examples, to end users in China or Macau, subject to conditions. The rule takes effect on January 15, 2026.

writer.headline: Bureau of Industry and Security final rule on AI chip licensing to China, Macau
writer.body: On January 15, 2026, the Bureau of Industry and Security issued a final rule providing case-by-case review for certain exports from the United States of chips below specified performance and memory-bandwidth limits to end users in China or Macau. Those exports are subject to conditions including independent US testing. The rule took effect on January 15, 2026.

card.headline: Bureau of Industry and Security final rule on AI chip licensing to China, Macau
card.body: On January 15, 2026, the Bureau of Industry and Security issued a final rule providing case-by-case review for certain exports from the United States of chips below specified performance and memory-bandwidth limits to end users in China or Macau. Those exports are subject to conditions including independent US testing. The rule took effect on January 15, 2026.
